### 🐛 Describe the bug\
\
### Summary\
\
Starting with vLLM 0.25.1, a large **dense** model (e.g. `Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct` FP8, TP=8) that previously started fine now OOMs during CUDA graph capture (`capture_model()`), even with an otherwise-unchanged config.\
\
The regression is caused by the interaction of two things:\
\
1. **Model Runner V2 is now the default for dense models.**\
2. **The V2 runner's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` is a dummy that returns `0`**, so the memory profiler reserves **no** headroom for CUDA graph capture. The KV cache is then sized to consume the entire `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, and `capture_model()` later OOMs when it allocates the CUDA graph buffers.\
\
The legacy (V1) runner implements `profile_cudagraph_memory()` properly and reserves this memory (≈9.5 GiB for this config), which is why the same config works on 0.23.0.\
\
### Root cause (with references to current `main`)\
\
**(a) V2 is selected by default for dense models** — `vllm/config/vllm.py`, `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` → `_is_default_v2_model_runner_model()`:\
\
```\
architectures = getattr(model_config, "architectures", [])\
return (\
    any(arch in DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES for arch in architectures)\
    or not model_config.is_moe\
)\
```\
\
For a dense model like `LlamaForCausalLM`, `is_moe` is `False`, so this returns `True` and V2 is selected when `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is unset (its default). In 0.23.0, the equivalent logic also fell back to the legacy runner for **quantized** models, so FP8 Llama used the V1 runner and was unaffected.\
\
**(b) The V2 runner does not actually profile CUDA graph memory** — `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`:\
\
```\
def profile_cudagraph_memory(self) -> int:\
    # NOTE(woosuk): It is TBD whether we keep this API or not.\
    return 0\
```\
\
This dummy was added in **PR [#36520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36520)** ("\[Model Runner V2\] Add dummy `profile_cudagraph_memory` API", commit `6e956d9eca398005929d29f123607d1029800cc7`) two days after **PR [#30515](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30515)** ("\[UX\]\[Startup\] Account for CUDA graphs during memory profiling") introduced the caller. It was a placeholder to satisfy the new interface and has never been implemented; it is still `return 0` on `main`.\
\
**(c) The worker subtracts this (zero) estimate when sizing the KV cache** — `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`, `determine_available_memory()`:\
\
```\
if (\
    current_platform.is_cuda_alike()\
    and self.vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode != CUDAGraphMode.NONE\
):\
    cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory()\
...\
cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied = (\
    cudagraph_memory_estimate\
    if envs.VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS  # default True\
    else 0\
)\
...\
self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes = (\
    self.requested_memory\
    - profile_result.non_kv_cache_memory\
    - cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied  # == 0 for the V2 runner\
)\
```\
\
With `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=True` (the default) but the V2 estimate being `0`, the KV cache claims the entire remaining budget. There is then no room left for the CUDA graph buffers allocated during `capture_model()`, and startup OOMs. On GPUs without NVLink (e.g. L40S) the extra NCCL buffer pressure makes this more likely to manifest.\
\
### Steps to reproduce (minimal, vLLM-native)\
\
```\
from vllm import LLM\
\
# Dense FP8 checkpoint, tensor-parallel across GPUs.\
# Reproduced on 8x L40S (no NVLink).\
llm = LLM(\
    model="<dense FP8 Llama-3.1-70B checkpoint>",\
    tensor_parallel_size=8,\
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.90,\
)\
```\
\
- **0.23.0:** starts successfully (legacy runner reserves CUDA graph memory).\
- **0.25.1 / `main`:** OOMs during CUDA graph capture.\
- Setting `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` on 0.25.1 makes it start successfully again.\
\
### Observed error (representative — please replace with your full traceback)\
\
```\
RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error (run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for details)\
...\
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate ...\
  (raised during capture_model() / CUDA graph capture at startup)\
```\
\
### Expected behavior\
\
CUDA graph capture memory should be reserved before the KV cache is sized, regardless of which model runner is selected, so that startup does not OOM on a config that fits with the legacy runner.\
\
### Workarounds\
\
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` — forces the legacy runner, which reserves CUDA graph memory correctly. (Preferred; keeps CUDA graphs enabled.)\
- Lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` to manually leave headroom.\
- `enforce_eager=True` — disables CUDA graphs entirely (perf cost).\
\
### Suggested fix\
\
Implement `profile_cudagraph_memory()` in the V2 runner (mirroring the legacy runner's implementation) so `determine_available_memory()` reserves the correct headroom. Alternatively, until the V2 API is implemented, either (a) account for CUDA graph capture memory in the V2 KV-cache sizing path, or (b) do not make V2 the default for configurations where CUDA graph capture memory is significant.\
\
I'm happy to open a PR porting the legacy `profile_cudagraph_memory()` logic into the V2 runner if that's the preferred direction.\
\
### Before submitting a new issue...\
\
- Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.\

Hi [@njhill](https://github.com/njhill) [@yewentao256](https://github.com/yewentao256) [@WoosukKwon](https://github.com/WoosukKwon) — we have an additional reproduction and controlled validation for this issue.\
\
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro 861B (FP8, TP=4, EP=true) on B200 hardware reproduces the failure with the upstream vLLM image.\
- Model Runner V2 reports `profile_cudagraph_memory() == 0`; the KV cache is oversized by approximately 15 GiB, matching the measured CUDA-graph footprint. The failure surfaces as an FP4 MoE workspace OOM or engine-start timeout.\
